back: Pattern: 'be + past participle + -ing' (e.g., 'The monkey was seen climbing') [4].
Some verbs followed by -ing can use 'being + past participle' (e.g., 'I love being given presents') [4].
Verbs like dread, imagine, and recall followed by an -ing clause usually have no passive [4].
Pattern: 'be + past participle + to-infinitive' (e.g., 'Peter has been taught to sing') [4].
Possible for 'expect/propose + to-infinitive' (e.g., 'Changes are expected to be proposed') [4].
Verbs like (can't) bear, hate, and love with object + to-infinitive have no passive [4].
Pattern: 'verb + to be + past participle' (e.g., 'Fresh pasta started to be sold') [4].
Verbs like agree, aim, and want do NOT have corresponding meanings in active and passive (e.g., 'Petra wanted to help me' ≠ 'I wanted to be helped by Petra') [4].
